task:
Task: Classify grass and parthenium vegetation
Classify two land cover types—grass and parthenium—within a defined study area using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from January to February 2020. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes a suite of 12 vegetation indices (e.g., NDVI, EVI, SAVI), and generates three classification models: one using only spectral bands, one using only vegetation indices, and one combining both. The classifications are performed using an SVM (libsvm) classifier with RBF kernel, trained on sampled regions labeled by 'id'. Accuracy is assessed using confusion matrices and overall accuracy metrics for each model. Area statistics per class are computed and visualized as charts. Final classified maps for all three models are displayed on the map and exported to Google Drive.

task:
Task: Calculate potential productivity
Calculate the Potential Productivity (P) for Ficus indica in 2001 using daily meteorological and soil data. It derives temperature, precipitation, and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) from GLDAS, PERSIANN-CDR, and BESS datasets, aggregates them daily, and computes an Environmental Productivity Index (EPI) through a series of empirical expressions involving temperature indices (It), water index (Iw), and radiation index (Ip). The final output is a mean annual potential productivity raster in mg/ha/y, masked to zero where negative, and exported at 27.83 km resolution over a global latitudinal extent from -60° to 80°.

Identify flood-affected areas in 2017 by analyzing Sentinel-1 SAR imagery before and after a flooding event. It computes VV and VH backscatter differences, applies thresholding (upper >1.15 and lower <0.7) and spatial filtering (connected pixel count ≥8) to detect inundation, then refines results using slope from SRTM to exclude steep terrain. task:
Task: Detect flood extent using SAR backscatter change
Detect flooded areas in Mokwa Town, Niger Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria, by computing a Composite Flood Index (CFI) from pre- and post-flood Sentinel-1 GRD imagery. It selects VV and VH polarizations, converts dB-scale backscatter to linear scale, computes normalized backscatter drop (Δσ⁰/σ⁰) for both bands, combines them via weighted average (0.6×VV + 0.4×VH), applies a threshold (>0.30) to generate a binary flood mask, and quantifies flooded area (in hectares) and flooded building count using Google Open Buildings. Outputs include an interactive map with flood index visualization, legend, title panel, UI documentation panel, area statistics, and flooded building count.

task:
Task: Calculate annual SPI from ERA5-LAND precipitation
Compute the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) at annual time scale for each year from 1993 to 2023, using monthly total precipitation from ECMWF ERA5-LAND. It first aggregates monthly precipitation (converted from meters to millimeters), computes long-term (1993–2023) mean and standard deviation of monthly precipitation, then derives annual SPI as (annual_sum − 12×mean) / (stdDev × √12). Outputs are clipped raster layers of SPI per year (SPI_1993 through SPI_2023), visualized in GEE and exported to Google Drive as GeoTIFFs with a diverging color palette (−2 to +2), representing drought/wetness severity relative to the 31-year baseline.

Task: Detect development area change
Detect land surface change in a development area using temporal differences in Sentinel-1 VV backscatter. Outputs include a change intensity map, a time series line chart of median VV backscatter over the region, and exports the development area geometry to Cloud Storage in SHP format.

task:
Task: Calculate normalized wetness index
Calculate a normalized version of the Wetness Index (WET_OLI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a user-defined region. It first removes clouds and cloud shadows using pixel QA masking, computes MNDWI to mask out water bodies, then calculates the WET_OLI index using a linear combination of blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, and SWIR2 bands. The resulting wetness values are clipped to [-1, 1], then normalized to [0, 1] range using percentile-based min-max scaling over the study area. Outputs include the raw and normalized wetness rasters for visualization and analysis.

task:
Task: Identify urban expansion and renewal
Analyze land development intensity (LDI) using Landsat 7 TOA reflectance from 2008 and 2009 over a specific fishnet grid. It computes the ratio of near-infrared to red bands (B3/B1) for both years, calculates LDI as the ratio of post- to pre-development CLI, and identifies land development where LDI > 1.2. Using a prior urban mask (GAUD dataset), it distinguishes urban expansion (new development on non-urban areas) and urban renewal (development in existing urban zones). The results are filtered with NDWI and NDVI to exclude water and vegetation, cleaned with focal mode filtering, and clipped to the region of interest. Outputs include classified rasters for land development, urban expansion, and urban renewal, visualized with custom color schemes.

task:
Task: Downscale MODIS NDVI using Landsat NDVI
the workflow performs spatiotemporal fusion to enhance the spatial resolution of MODIS NDVI (500 m) to ~30 m by establishing a linear regression model between coincident Landsat-derived NDVI (30 m, from SR_B5/SR_B4) and MODIS NDVI (500 m) over a defined polygon in southwestern Iran. It filters Landsat 8 Collection 2 Tier 1 Surface Reflectance images by path/row (166/38), cloud cover (<10%), and date (2020–2021), applies radiometric calibration using per-band gain/offset coefficients, computes NDVI, joins with temporally proximate MODIS MOD09GA NDVI images (±3 days), fits a pixel-wise linear regression (MODIS NDVI → Landsat NDVI), then applies the derived gain and offset to all MODIS NDVI images to generate a sharpened 30-m NDVI time series ('ndvi30'). The output includes a clipped multiband image stack of sharpened NDVI and a time series chart of the predicted NDVI at a single point (48.2408°E, 32.3616°N).

task:
Task: Detect lantana camara presence
Detect potential Lantana camara infestation pixels in the Anamalai Hills (Tamil Nadu, India) using a spectral likelihood score (LLS) derived from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance. It combines three normalized spectral indicators — NDRE (B8/B5), NDVI (B8/B4), and inverted SWIR ratio (B11/B8) — weighted by empirical coefficients (0.40, 0.35, 0.25) to produce a continuous LLS raster. Detection is thresholded at LLS > 0.5, then constrained spatially using ESA WorldCover habitat classes (20=shrubs, 30=grassland, 40=cropland) and JRC Global Surface Water seasonality mask (excluding persistent water). The final binary lantana candidate layer is used to stratified-sample 150 presence points with geographic coordinates, species label, source, and year (2023), exported as CSV and Shapefile for field validation or modeling.

Task: Extract water bodies from SAR
Extract surface water bodies from Sentinel-1 GRD imagery using the S1-GNDPI index — a polarimetric SAR index computed from VV and VH backscatter channels. It applies speckle filtering (focal_median), converts dB to linear scale, computes the non-coherent sum (VV_linear + VH_linear), applies a natural logarithm and affine normalization (0.5·ln(sum) + 1.90), and outputs a continuous-index raster (S1_GNDPI) where water pixels (~−0.4) are dark and urban/land pixels (~1.9) are bright. The result is visualized as grayscale and pseudo-color layers over the ROI, with optional percentile statistics and export capability.

Task: Estimate aboveground biomass
Estimate annual aboveground biomass (AGB) for herbaceous and perennial forage groups from 2010 to 2019 using partitioned NPP data from the Rangeland Analysis Platform. It applies a temperature-dependent fraction model (fANPP) derived from mean annual temperature (MAT) to allocate NPP to aboveground components, converts units from NPP (kg C/m²) to biomass (lbs/acre), and computes total herbaceous AGB as the sum of functional group contributions. The output is a time-series of classified rasters, one per year, containing three biomass components (afgAGB, pfgAGB, herbaceousAGB), exported as 16-bit integers to Google Drive.

Task: Smooth and reconstruct NDVI time series
the workflow reconstructs and smooths MODIS NDVI time series data over Chongqing from 2014 to 2019 using a Savitzky-Golay-like filtering approach combined with kriged interpolation. It first clips MODIS/006/MOD13Q1 imagery to the Chongqing boundary, extracts NDVI and DetailedQA bands, and masks based on QA values. A smoothing function is applied using a least-squares polynomial fitting kernel derived from a predefined window size (M=5) and polynomial order (d=4), leveraging a pre-kriged NDVI image collection for temporal continuity. The final output combines original NDVI with smoothed results weighted by QA flags (0–3), producing a fused SG (smoothed gap-filled) NDVI product. Outputs include both the original and reconstructed NDVI layers visualized using a custom NDVI color palette.

Generate a cloud-optimized, median-based surface reflectance composite from Sentinel-2 Level-2A (SR) imagery over a defined polygonal region for the period 2023–2024. It applies dual cloud masking: (1) using the Scene Classification Layer (SCL) to exclude saturated/defective pixels (class 1), shadows (3), and cloud/cirrus classes (7–10), and (2) using the pixel-level cloud probability mask (MSK_CLDPRB) to retain only pixels with <20% cloud probability. The output is a 6-band clipped composite (B2, B3, B4, B8, B11, B12) used to generate four visualizations (true color, NIR, SWIR) and an NDVI layer (B8/B4), enabling qualitative and semi-quantitative assessment of surface reflectance properties, vegetation health, and land surface conditions.

task:
Task: Calculate THI under RCP45 scenario
Calculate the Temperature-Humidity Index (THI) using daily maximum and minimum temperature projections from the NASA NEX-GDDP dataset under the RCP45 climate scenario for the NorESM1-M model. It applies a masking function based on forest cover data from the Hansen dataset to restrict analysis to areas with valid land observations. Monthly THI values are computed, averaged over decadal time windows (e.g., 2010–2030, 2020–2040, etc.), and then used to compute signal-to-noise ratios by subtracting a reference period (refp) and dividing by noise. The final outputs are exported as global raster images of Time of Emergence (ToE) metrics at 50 km resolution, representing when significant deviations in THI emerge under climate change.

Task: Classify land cover change
Analyze changes in land cover between two time periods (2021 and 2022) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery. task:
Task: Estimate potential productivity for Ficus indica
Calculate the Environmental Productivity Index (EPI) to estimate potential agricultural productivity for *Ficus indica* (fig tree) in arid and arable regions. It uses daily meteorological data (air temperature, precipitation, and photosynthetically active radiation) from GLDAS, PERSIANN-CDR, and BESS datasets over 2019, aggregates them by day, computes temperature and radiation efficiency indices (It, Ip), integrates soil water availability (Iw) via USDA soil texture-derived gamma index (gi), and multiplies with a native pmax layer (Nat_pmax_arid_arable). The final output is a mean annual EPI raster representing modeled productivity in mg/ha/y, masked to valid areas and exported globally at 27.83 km resolution.

Compute a continuous, harmonized NDVI time series from 1982 to 2024 using calibrated surface reflectance data from Landsat 4–9 over a fixed WRS path/row (165/38) and user-defined polygon ROI in southwestern Iran. It applies sensor-specific band ratios (B4/B3 for TM/ETM+, B5/B4 for OLI), radiometric calibration (scale factor 0.0000275 + offset −0.2), cloud filtering (<45% cloud cover), and SLC-off gap-filling for Landsat 7 (2003–present) using focal median blending. Outputs include: (1) an interactive time-series chart of mean NDVI over the ROI, (2) a clipped, multi-temporal NDVI image stack (as bands) for 2010–2011 exported to Google Drive, and (3) a merged, chronologically sorted ImageCollection for further analysis.

task:
Task: Analyze forest kNDVI change
Compute and compares kernel-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (kNDVI) values for forested areas in a custom polygonal region of interest (ROI) between the years 2000 and 2023. It first defines a closed polygon from 25 coordinate pairs (likely spanning parts of South America, given longitude/latitude ranges: ~−19° to 54°N, ~−37° to 19°S), clips Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC) data to extract forest cover ≥25% canopy in 2000 and persistent forest (i.e., unchanged forest pixels that remained forested from 2000 through 2023, masked using GFC 'treecover2000' and 'loss'). It then applies this unchanged-forest mask to two precomputed kNDVI image composites — one for 2000 (aggregated from four user-uploaded subregion assets) and one for 2023 (aggregated from four distinct user-uploaded subregion assets, each hosted under different user accounts). Finally, it computes the mean kNDVI value per 5 km × 5 km grid cell (from a user-provided Fishnet feature collection) over the unchanged forest area and exports the results as a CSV table containing mean kNDVI_2000 and kNDVI_2023 per grid cell.

The final output is a FeatureCollection of grid cells with attached LST statistics, exported as a Shapefile ('Tehran_LST_Day_Night.shp') to Google Drive.

task:
Task: Model nighttime lights trend
Compute a linear regression trend (slope, intercept, and residual) of calibrated DMSP-OLS nighttime lights (avg_vis band) over time, using years since 1990 as the independent variable. Task: Compute annual NBR time series

Task: Model precipitation trend over time
the workflow models the linear trend of precipitation (pr_mean) over time using climate projection data from the NASA NEX-DCP30 ensemble under the RCP8.5 scenario for 2006–2050. It adds a scaled time band (system:time_start) to each image, then applies ee.Reducer.linearFit() to regress precipitation against time — producing three output bands: 'scale' (slope, i.e., mm/year change in precipitation), 'offset' (y-intercept), and a second 'scale' band (redundant due to select order; likely intended as correlation or residual, but per GEE linearFit spec, it outputs [scale, offset, scale, offset] for two-band input — here only first two are meaningful; the visualization uses 'scale', 'offset', 'scale' for RGB). The result is a global (or dataset-native spatial extent) raster layer representing the linear rate of change (trend slope), baseline intercept, and again slope — visualized with custom min/max scaling.

Task: Assess vegetation performance degradation
the workflow assesses vegetation productivity performance over time in the Kiteto and Kongwa regions using Landsat surface reflectance data from 1999 to 2019. It computes NDVI, applies atmospheric and radiometric corrections (including sensor cross-calibration between ETM+, OLI, and TM), masks clouds and shadows, and derives baseline (1999–2015) and comparison (2015–2019) mean NDVI composites. Using soil and land cover data to define eco-units, it calculates the 90th percentile of NDVI per unit as a reference maximum, then computes a performance ratio (observed/max) for each period. Degradation is identified where performance drops below 0.5. Outputs include raster layers for performance baselines/comparisons, degradation maps, and a histogram showing pixel count distribution of performance ratios.

task:
Task: Estimate runoff from rainfall and land cover
Estimate daily surface runoff over a watershed using the SCS-CN method. It derives Curve Number (CN2) values by combining MODIS-based land use/land cover (LC_Type1) and OpenLandMap soil texture classes, reclassified into hydrologic soil groups. Daily CHIRPS rainfall data are used to compute antecedent moisture conditions (AMC) over a 5-day window, which dynamically adjusts potential retention (S) via CN1, CN2, and CN3 transformations. Runoff is calculated using a piecewise expression based on precipitation and variable S values under AMC I, II, and III conditions. The output includes time-series images of rainfall-runoff pairs, cumulative rainfall and runoff maps, and a chart of mean daily rainfall and runoff over the AOI for hydrological analysis.

Task: Map snow cover duration
Map the duration of snow cover over a region of interest (ROI) defined by a point location in Iran (coordinates [24.852, 60.258]) intersected with FAO GAUL level-1 administrative boundaries. It loads MODIS MOD10A1 NDSI Snow Cover data for 2023–2024, applies a temporal join-based smoothing using a 7-day window and the 75th percentile reducer to suppress noise and cloud artifacts, then thresholds the smoothed NDSI values (>40) to generate binary snow/no-snow images, and finally sums these binary images across time to produce a snow duration raster (number of days with snow cover). Outputs include: (1) a time-series chart of mean smoothed NDSI over the ROI, (2) a clipped smoothed NDSI image stack, and (3) a clipped integer raster representing cumulative snow-covered days.

task:
Task: Correct SAR incidence angle to Gamma0
the workflow corrects Sentinel-1 GRD backscatter (Sigma0) to Gamma0 by applying an incidence angle correction using the radar geometry stored in the 'angle' band. It computes Gamma0 as Sigma0 − 10·log₁₀(cos(θ)), where θ is the local incidence angle in radians, leveraging the standard radiometric terrain correction approximation for terrain-flattened backscatter. The workflow processes two monthly composites (November 2015 and January 2016) of HH-polarized, descending-orbit, IW-mode Sentinel-1 GRD data, maps the correction function over each collection, then computes mean composites before and after correction. Outputs are four visualized layers: Sigma0 and Gamma0 for both time periods, enabling comparative analysis of radiometrically consistent backscatter over time.

task:
Task: Compare forest loss in protected areas
Analyze tree cover and forest loss within Malawi's protected areas, categorized by IUCN protection level. It samples 1000 random pixels within this region, extracts their SST values along with latitude and longitude, and converts them into point features. Kriging interpolation is then applied to these sampled points using an exponential model to predict SST across the region, producing a continuous surface. The results are visualized alongside the original raster and sample points using a custom color palette. Outputs include the interpolated SST surface, the raw SST image, and the sample point feature collection for comparison.

Task: Estimate soil moisture from LST and NDVI
Estimate surface soil moisture using a vegetation-index-based temperature-vegetation dryness index (TVDI-like) approach. It processes Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance (SR) and Surface Temperature (ST) bands to compute NDVI and LST, then derives two endmembers — full vegetation cover (high NDVI ≥ 0.3) and bare land (NDVI ∈ [0, 0.2)) — to estimate the wet (vw) and dry (vd) edges of the LST–NDVI trapezoid for vegetated pixels, and the wet (iw) and dry (id) edges for bare land. Using these empirical bounds, it computes soil moisture via an analytical expression that linearly interpolates within the trapezoidal space. Outputs include a time-series chart of mean soil moisture over the ROI and a masked, clipped, multi-temporal soil moisture image stack exported to Google Drive.

task:
Task: Model thermal stress emergence
the workflow models the emergence of thermal stress under the RCP85 climate scenario using NASA NEX-GDDP data for the CSIRO-Mk3-6-0 model. It calculates the mean temperature (THI) from daily maximum and minimum temperatures (tasmax, tasmin), converts them from Kelvin to Celsius, and computes a standardized anomaly (sr) relative to a baseline (inicial) and maximum dispersion (dis_max). Thresholds at 30%, 50%, 80%, and 100% of this anomaly are used to define vulnerability (vu), endangerment (en), crisis (cr), and collapse (co) levels. For each year from 2016 to 2089, binary maps are generated indicating when thresholds are exceeded, then remapped with the respective year value. The earliest year of threshold exceedance is determined via min reduction across time, producing four output rasters showing the first occurrence of each stress level. These are exported as global images at 30 km resolution.

Task: Fuse Sentinel-2 and MODIS reflectance
the workflow fuses Sentinel-2 and MODIS surface reflectance data to reconstruct a predicted Sentinel-2-like image (S3) for a target date using temporal interpolation based on MODIS time series. It computes S3 as S2 + (MOD3 - MOD2), where S2 is the observed Sentinel-2 image from an earlier date, and MOD3/MOD2 are smoothed MODIS Nadir Reflectance Band1 values at the target and earlier dates. The output includes the reconstructed S3 image, the original S3 image (S3original), and a validation layer showing the difference between them, visualized with a custom color palette to assess reconstruction accuracy.

task:
Task: Detect mangrove damage from flood
Detect mangrove damage caused by flooding during Hurricane Irma using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery. It computes a pre-event VH-polarized backscatter median composite, mosaics post-event VH images (2017-09-10 to 2017-09-13), calculates the difference (VHdiff), masks non-water areas, and identifies flooded regions where the drop in backscatter exceeds a threshold (VHdiff > 3). The resulting flood extent is used to mask a mangrove damage image, which is then aggregated over grid cells to compute area of damaged mangroves per region. Outputs include visualizations of false-color composites, median/VH difference layers, binary flood map, and a CSV export of mangrove damage statistics per grid.

Task: Detect ghost infrastructure using utilization index
Detect 'ghost infrastructure' — built-up areas with low or no human activity — by computing an Infrastructure Utilization Index (IUI) as the pixel-wise product of three normalized, co-registered geospatial indicators: (1) Sentinel-2–derived built-up index (SWIR–NIR normalized difference using B11 and B8), (2) VIIRS night-time lights intensity (avg_rad), and (3) Landsat-based temporal NDVI variability (standard deviation over 2015–2024). It then applies unsupervised Weka K-Means clustering (k=3) on these three features to identify clusters representing high-utilization, low-utilization, and ghost (built-up but dark & temporally static) infrastructure. Outputs include visualized layers for each intermediate metric and a final clustered map labeled 'AI Ghost Infrastructure Clusters', where red/yellow/green correspond to underutilized/ghost/high-utilization classes.

task:
Task: Compute 2100 aridity and climate classification
Compute the 2100 climatology (monthly and annual) of precipitation (PR), maximum/minimum temperature (TASMAX/TASMIN) from NASA/NEX-GDDP under RCP85, converts temperatures to °C, calculates Hamon potential evapotranspiration (PET) using mean temperature and extraterrestrial radiation, derives the Aridity Index (AI = P_ann / PET_ann), classifies aridity into five categories (hyperarid, arid, semiarid, monsoon, Mediterranean) based on AI thresholds and high-sun season precipitation ratio (April–September), and corrects monsoon/Mediterranean labels for Southern Hemisphere seasonality. The final output is a global raster map (clim2100_flip) of future climate classes (0–5) with a custom palette for visualization.

Task: Classify deforestation in Laos
the workflow models and classifies deforestation patterns in Laos using a Random Forest classifier trained on multi-temporal geospatial variables. It combines version 20 loss data (v20_loss) from 2010–2014 with terrain (ALOS DEM, slope), proximity features (roads, villages), population density (GPWv4), forest cover metrics (PRIM, TCC), spectral differences (lastFirstDiff, indexDiff), fire occurrences (FIRMS), precipitation (GSMaP), and spatial autocorrelation layers (Geary’s, GLCM). The training uses stratified sampling on merged 2014 loss data from Hansen and local product, and the final output is a classified deforestation map for 2013 exported as an asset.

task:
Task: Detect river encroachment
Compute MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index) water masks from Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance imagery for the Dhaka river system (Buriganga, Turag, Balu, and Shitalakshya rivers) to detect anthropogenic encroachment — specifically, loss of river surface area between 2016–2017 (dry season baseline) and 2025–2026 (current dry season). It applies cloud masking using QA60 bits 10 and 11, resamples SWIR-1 (B11) to 10m via bilinear interpolation, thresholds MNDWI at >0.0 to generate binary water masks, then identifies encroachment as pixels that were water in 2016 but non-water in 2026. Outputs include: (1) continuous MNDWI rasters for both periods; (2) binary water masks; (3) encroachment/erosion raster layers; (4) quantitative area statistics (in m²) for water extent and encroached area; and (5) exportable GeoTIFF and GeoJSON (for Buriganga segment) of encroachment polygons.

Task: Estimate soil moisture from Sentinel-1 VV

It applies speckle filtering (3×3 focal_mean), radiometric terrain flattening using local LiDAR-derived topographic correction (subtracting scaled LiDAR DSM), and dynamic min-max normalization (0–100 scale) computed per bi-weekly image over the AOI. Outputs include: (1) clipped, normalized VV backscatter mosaics visualized in Google Earth Engine with a blue→red palette; (2) georeferenced GeoTIFF exports to Google Drive (10 m resolution, EPSG:4326) named by year_month_half (e.g., '2021_05_1'), each representing a bi-weekly soil moisture proxy for the AOI.

Task: Compute modified soil adjusted vegetation index
Compute the Modified Soil Adjusted Vegetation Index (MSAVI) and a Spectral Index (SI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery over China for summer months in 2017 and 2018. It combines two image collections, applies cloud filtering, calculates SI as sqrt(B2 * B4), derives MSAVI through a non-linear transformation involving B4 (Red) and B5 (NIR), normalizes both indices (G_SI, G_MSAVI), and finally computes a combined Multi-Index (MSI) as the Euclidean distance from a reference point. Outputs include mapped layers of SI, MSAVI, G_SI, G_MSAVI, and MSI, along with region-reduced min/max statistics for SI and MSAVI. The final MSI raster is exported to Google Drive.

task:
Task: Assess forest health change
the workflow performs modal analysis to assess overall forest health change between 2017 and 2021 across India’s agroclimatic regions, using two precomputed change layers — CCD (Continuous Change Detection) and CHM (Canopy Height Model) change — derived from time-series satellite data. It combines them via a rule-based decision logic to classify pixels into seven categories: Deforestation (-2), Degradation (-1), No Change (0), Improvement (1), Afforestation (2), Partially Degraded (3 or 4, depending on directionality of CCD vs CHM change), and Missing Data (5). The output is a clipped, masked raster ‘overall_change’ with categorical integer values, visualized with a custom legend and optionally exportable to Earth Engine Assets. Pixel counts for selected change classes (currently [-1, 3, 4]) are computed by gridding the AOI at 100 km resolution and aggregating 25 m pixel counts per grid cell, then converting to km² (625 m² per 25 m pixel → ×625 ÷ 10⁶ = km²).

Task: Compare ERA5 daily Tmax datasets for glacier warm-season analysis
the workflow evaluates two GEE-hosted ERA5 daily climate datasets — 'ECMWF/ERA5/DAILY' and 'ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR' — for suitability in computing glacier extreme-warm indicators (e.g., warm-season daily maximum temperature counts). For a user-specified region (e.g., 'central_asia'), it extracts per-year metadata including: (1) number of available images during warm months, (2) first and last image timestamps, (3) band names present, (4) existence and value of annual mean daily maximum air temperature (converted from Kelvin to Celsius) at a representative point, and (5) whether the Tmax-like band remains populated across 2019–2024. Outputs are printed as FeatureCollections — one per dataset — containing annual diagnostic features with flags and metrics; no final raster or map product is generated — only tabular diagnostics for dataset selection.

Task: Identify urban areas using NDBI
Identify urbanized areas in Puyang using Sentinel-2 imagery from December 2020 to March 2021. It applies cloud masking based on the QA60 band and filters images with less than 5% cloud cover. A median composite is created, followed by computation of NDBI (Normalized Difference Built-up Index) using bands B12 and B8. The qualityMosaic is then generated using NDBI to select the 'blackest' (most built-up) pixels, and MNDWI and NDVI are also calculated. Finally, the NDBI layer is clipped to the region of interest (roi) and exported as a raster to Google Drive for urban area analysis.

Task: Map high carbon sequestration zones
Identify spatially explicit high carbon sequestration zones across the United Arab Emirates by integrating three biophysical indicators: (1) NDVI-derived vegetation vigor from Sentinel-2 (B8/B4), (2) soil organic carbon concentration from OpenLandMap (b0), and (3) annual net primary productivity from MODIS MCD17A3HGF (Npp). It computes a dynamic NDVI threshold (mean + 0.5×stdDev) over UAE, masks NDVI to retain only pixels above that threshold, then intersects it with soil carbon (>1.5 kg/m²) and NPP (>500 gC/m²/yr) layers via sequential masking. Outputs include: (a) a final binary raster of high-sequestration zones (magenta visualization), (b) per-pixel NDVI statistics (mean, stdDev, threshold), (c) sampled NDVI values at ground-truth carbon points, and (d) layered visualizations of all input and derived products for validation and interpretation.

task:
Task: Estimate daily runoff using SCS-CN method
Estimate spatially explicit daily surface runoff (in mm) for the Shipra River basin in Ujjain, India, over a one-year period (2019–2020), using the Soil Conservation Service Curve Number (SCS-CN) method. It dynamically adjusts the initial abstraction ratio and S-value based on antecedent moisture conditions (AMC I/II/III) derived from 5-day cumulative CHIRPS rainfall. Inputs include MODIS-derived LULC (MCD12Q1 LC_Type1), OpenLandMap soil texture (converted to USDA hydrologic soil groups A–D), and CHIRPS daily precipitation. The workflow computes CN2 (baseline curve number), derives CN1 and CN3, calculates corresponding S-values (potential retention), selects the appropriate S-value per pixel per day based on AMC classification, and applies the standard SCS-CN runoff equation — with zero-runoff thresholding (P < 0.2S). Outputs include: (1) daily runoff rasters clipped to the AOI; (2) summed annual rainfall and runoff maps; (3) time-series chart of mean rainfall and runoff over the AOI.

Finally, it extracts pixel values from both collections at sample locations, merges them into a single feature collection with synchronized dates and vegetation metrics, and exports the combined dataset as a shapefile for external analysis.

Task: Extract NDVI and RGB percentiles
Generate a composite image from Sentinel-2 data by first filtering images with less than 95% cloud cover and applying a cloud mask. It computes NDVI using bands B8 and B4, then creates a final composite by selecting the maximum value across the collection as baseline. Subsequently, it refines the composite by incorporating the 35th percentile of blue (B2), green (B3), and red (B4) bands and the 90th percentile of NDVI from pixels below a low reflectance threshold (0.23) to reduce residual cloud and bright pixel contamination. The output is a surface-reflectance-corrected, cloud-masked, percentile-based composite image with enhanced vegetation and RGB information for visual interpretation and analysis.

task:
Task: Model active layer thickness
the workflow models the Active Layer Thickness (ALT) of the Tibetan Plateau (TP) using MODIS LST data from 2006 to 2020 and climate projections from NASA/NEX-GDDP under the rcp85 scenario for future periods. It computes mean annual ground temperature from day/night land surface temperatures, applies a square-root-based thermal model (ALT = E × √∑T), extrapolates ALT into the future using tasmin from GCMs (ACCESS1-0), and generates a time series chart of ALT from 2006 to 2099. The final output includes a mapped ALT estimate for 2099 under RCP85 and regional mean values printed and exported.

Task: Quantify urban heat island intensity
the workflow quantifies the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect in Hanoi, Vietnam, by computing Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 8 Collection 2 Tier 1 Level 2 surface temperature band (ST_B10) for September of each year from 2013 to 2023. It defines two concentric zones — urban core (0–10 km radius around Hoàn Kiếm Lake) and suburban ring (10–15 km) — applies cloud and cloud shadow masking using QA_PIXEL bit flags, computes annual median LST per zone, derives zone-specific mean and standard deviation statistics, calculates inter-zonal temperature difference (ΔT = urban_mean − suburban_mean) annually, and outputs: (1) time-series charts of mean LST for urban and suburban zones; (2) a UHI intensity time-series chart; (3) a CSV table listing annual image counts and metadata; (4) a comprehensive CSV with yearly urban/suburban LST means, standard deviations, and ΔT; and (5) GeoTIFF exports of visualized LST maps (20–45°C range, custom thermal palette) for each year, clipped to the combined urban–suburban extent.

Task: Classify forest degradation using multispectral ratios
Classify forest degradation in a tropical region using Landsat-derived spectral indices and band ratios from two time periods (2012 and 2016). It computes simple composites for Landsat 7 and Landsat 8, selects consistent bands across sensors, calculates multiple band ratios (e.g., B4/B5, B5/B7), and generates NDVI. These features are combined into a multi-temporal stack, trained with a Random Forest classifier using labeled sample points (degradation vs. stable forest), and applied to produce a probability-based degradation map. The output includes a classified raster of degradation levels and a derived CO2 loss proxy layer, both exported to Drive.

task:
Task: Assess flood vulnerability level
the workflow assesses flood vulnerability in a study area using a weighted overlay model combining elevation, land use/land cover (LULC), flow accumulation, and precipitation data derived from remote sensing. It first classifies LULC using Landsat 8 OLI surface reflectance imagery and a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined feature collections. Then, it generates suitability scores for each factor: elevation (DEM) is classified into low, medium, and high risk; LULC is assigned risk weights based on land cover types; flow accumulation from HydroSHEDS determines drainage potential; and long-term CHIRPS precipitation data is used to compute zonal thresholds for rainfall risk. These scored layers are combined with weighted summation (DEM: 20%, LULC: 25%, Flow: 25%, Precipitation: 30%) to produce a final flood vulnerability index. This index is reclassified into three levels—Not Vulnerable, Vulnerable, and Highly Vulnerable—and visualized on the map with a legend. The output is a classified raster map of flood vulnerability levels and associated statistics over the area of interest.

Task: Classify rice cultivation area
Classify rice cultivation areas in the BWN region using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from 2016. It filters and processes VV and VH polarized C-band backscatter data from descending IW mode passes, applies temporal compositing for specific growth stages (September–October 2016), and performs spatial filtering using a boxcar convolution. A Classification and Regression Tree (CART) classifier is trained on VV band values from labeled sample regions (rice vs. non-rice), then applied to a later-stage image (stage_G) to generate a binary rice classification map. The result is masked to extract only rice-predicted pixels, and the total cropland area is computed in hectares via pixel area summation within the BWN boundary. Outputs include the classified raster map, a masked extraction of predicted rice areas, and the estimated agricultural extent in hectares.

Generate and visualizes median cloud-masked, atmospherically corrected surface reflectance composites for three distinct satellite systems (Landsat 9, Landsat 5 TM, and Sentinel-2) over the same geographic area (HGO_study_area and Atlapexco) during May periods across three decades (1986, 2022, and 2020–2023). It produces true-color visualizations (RGB: B4-B3-B2 for Sentinel; SR_B4-SR_B3-SR_B2 for Landsat 9; SR_B3-SR_B2-SR_B1 for Landsat 5) and exports the Sentinel-2 composite clipped to the 'Atlapexco' boundary (a drainage or administrative unit) at 10 m resolution. The workflow includes cloud masking (via SCL band for Sentinel-2 and CLOUD_COVER metadata for Landsat), temporal filtering (May-only, multi-year windows), spatial clipping, band subsetting ('SR_B.*|ST.*' and 'B4,B3,B2'), scaling (toInt16), and median compositing — enabling cross-sensor, cross-era qualitative comparison of land surface spectral response.

task:
Task: Estimate chlorophyll-a concentration
Estimate chlorophyll-a and phycocyanin concentrations in surface water using Sentinel-2 MSI imagery. It computes the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) and a phyco-based index from top-of-atmosphere reflectance bands, applies cloud masking, filters images by date and cloud cover, and calculates mean composites for two time periods (2017–2019 and 2019–2021). Water bodies are masked using NDWI with a threshold of 0.1. The resulting chlorophyll-a layers are smoothed using a circular convolution kernel and visualized on a split-panel map centered on a user-defined geometry. Outputs include time-composited, spatially-smoothed chlorophyll-a rasters for both periods, interactive inspection tools, and an export to Earth Engine Assets.

Task: Detect vegetation loss using SAR
Detect vegetation loss in a study area using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR imagery by analyzing changes in VH polarization backscatter over time. It processes VV and VH polarized images from descending passes, applies temporal filtering via focal mean smoothing, computes multi-temporal differences (2016–2018 and 2018–2019), thresholds the difference to identify significant backscatter increases (indicative of vegetation loss), masks and maps the change areas, and calculates zonal statistics including mean, standard deviation, and total loss area. Outputs include filtered SAR mosaics, difference layers, thresholded change maps, histograms, and numerical summaries of change extent.

task:
Task: Compute TVMDI index
Compute the Temperature-Vegetation-Moisture Dryness Index (TVMDI) by combining normalized time-series MODIS-derived land surface temperature (LST), vegetation condition (PVI), and moisture condition (SM) over a specified geometry. Each variable is scaled using min-max normalization multiplied by a coefficient (0.57735), then combined into a composite index image through band-wise algebraic operations: sqrt(SM² + LST² - PVI² + 0.33), with final clamping between 0 and 1. The output is a single-layer raster representing dryness conditions, which is visualized on the map and exported to Google Drive at 1000m resolution.

Task: Predict bare ground cover

Outputs include mapped predictions, accuracy assessment charts, and feature importance analysis.

Identify surface water extent in a reservoir area using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from December 2021 to January 2022. It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, filters images by cloud cover, and computes the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) using Green (B3) and NIR (B8) bands. The workflow includes clipping to a reservoir boundary, masking clouds and cirrus, filtering valid pixels, and generating an NDWI time series. Outputs include a filtered image collection, cloud-masked composites, and an NDWI raster stack for visualizing surface water patterns.

task:
Task: Derive seasonal land surface temperature
Compute seasonal Land Surface Temperature (LST) composites for a rectangular AOI in the Netherlands (approx. 6.84°–6.88°E, 52.23°–52.25°N) from Landsat 8 Collection 2 Tier 1 Level 2 surface temperature band (ST_B10). It applies cloud and cloud shadow masking using QA_PIXEL bits 3 and 5, converts thermal radiance to Kelvin using the scale factor 0.00341802 and offset 149.0, then converts to Celsius (°C), clips to the AOI, and computes mean LST per season (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall) for each year from 2021 to 2024. Outputs include 16 individual seasonal LST composite images (4 seasons × 4 years) and one overall mean LST composite across all seasons and years — visualized with a blue-white-red palette ranging from −10 °C to 40 °C.

task:
Task: Assess wildfire severity using dNBR
the workflow assesses wildfire severity in a tropical region by computing the differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) from Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery before and after a fire event. It uses FIRMS thermal alerts to identify active fires between November 2019 and January 2020, then processes pre- and post-fire Sentinel-2 images clipped to the affected area, applies cloud masking via QA60, and calculates NBR for both periods. The dNBR is derived by subtracting post-fire NBR from pre-fire NBR, classified into burn severity levels using thresholding, and exported as a raster. Outputs include visualizations of fire activity, pre/post false-color composites, NBR layers, classified dNBR map, and two exported GeoTIFFs: one for classified severity and one for continuous dNBR values.

Task: Assess landslide risk using rainfall and wind forecasts
the workflow assesses landslide risk over a region by combining a soil index (SI), three-day accumulated rainfall, and three-day-ahead precipitation and wind forecasts. It applies a decision tree model based on threshold rules derived from scientific literature (e.g., Rui Marques) to classify areas into Moderate, High, and Very High risk levels. The output includes four daily landslide risk maps (for tomorrow, day after tomorrow, third day, and a Hurricane Ophelia example case), each masked to exclude low-risk areas (value ≤1), and interactive UI controls for visualization with legends and optional overlay layers (subsidence, soil moisture, NDVI, rainfall, wind).

task:
Task: Compute vegetation condition index
Compute the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Precipitation Condition Index (PCI), and Soil Moisture Condition Index (SMCI) using MODIS NDVI, MODIS LST, TRMM precipitation, and FLDAS soil moisture data for 2022. It first retrieves and visualizes NDVI, then calculates VCI by normalizing NDVI values between seasonal min and max. Similarly, it processes LST to derive TCI with an inverse relationship to temperature, while PCI and SMCI are computed from normalized precipitation and soil moisture values. All indices are scaled from 0 to 100 and added as new bands. The outputs include mapped layers of NDVI, VCI, LST, TCI, PCI, and SMCI with appropriate color palettes for visualization in Earth Engine.

task:
Task: Identify flood-vulnerable areas
Identify flood-vulnerable areas by integrating Sentinel-1 SAR (VV polarization) backscatter time series and SRTM-derived terrain slope to detect low-lying, flat regions (slope < 5°) exhibiting SAR signatures consistent with surface water or saturation (VV < −16 dB) — either persistently across two periods (Jan–Mar vs Apr–Jun 2020) or specifically in the later period. It outputs two binary raster layers: (1) 'Áreas Vulnerables (Planas y con Agua P1 o P2)' — flat areas with SAR-indicated water in either period, and (2) 'Áreas Vulnerables (Planas y con Agua P2)' — flat areas with SAR-indicated water only in the second period (interpreted as recent or event-triggered inundation potential).

task:
Task: Cluster land cover classes
the workflow performs an unsupervised classification to identify distinct land cover types within a user-defined study area using median composite Landsat 8 TOA reflectance imagery from the first half of 2015. It applies cloud masking using the BQA band, computes a median reduction across the image collection, and extracts spectral bands (B2–B7) for clustering. A wekaKMeans clusterer with 15 classes is trained on 10,000 random pixels sampled from the study area, and the resulting model classifies the entire area into 15 spectral clusters. The output includes a classified raster map displayed with a manually defined color legend for each cluster, visualized in false-color composite, and added to the map interface for interpretation.

Task: Extract NDVI time series
Extract and processes MODIS NDVI time series data from 2018 to 2022 over a user-defined region (table). It applies quality filtering using the SummaryQA band to retain only high-quality pixels (quality flags 0 and 1), rescales NDVI values by multiplying by 0.0001, and computes mean NDVI values per geometry via reduceRegion. task:
Task: Estimate soil moisture from SAR
Estimate surface soil moisture (SSM) using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR data by normalizing VV backscatter for incidence angle effects and scaling between empirically derived dry and wet references. It computes a linear regression between VV and incidence angle to generate beta, applies angular normalization to create VVnorm, identifies minimum (driest) and maximum (wettest) conditions over time, calculates sensitivity as their difference, and converts VVnorm values into volumetric soil moisture (0.20–0.35 m³/m³). Outputs include time-series charts of backscatter, normalized VV, and SSM over regions of interest, interactive mapping of SSM with chart-click visualization, and median VV composite; the final output is a Soil Surface Moisture (SSM) image collection mapped over time.

Task: Assess wildfire severity using dNBR
the workflow assesses wildfire severity for the 'DEVIL' fire event using pre- and post-fire Sentinel-2 imagery. It computes the normalized burn ratio (NBR) for both periods, calculates the difference (dNBR), and classifies burn severity into eight classes (e.g., High Severity, Unburned, Enhanced Regrowth). A custom SLD-based visualization is applied to map dNBR, and a legend with class descriptions is added. task:
Task: Model land cover change over time
the workflow implements a Bayesian Updating of Land Cover (BULC) model to analyze land cover change over multiple time steps using a sequence of classified land cover images. It initializes with a base land cover image from 2000 and processes a time series of event images (including K-means clustered classifications and Copernicus-derived layers) from 2014 to 2018. The workflow computes transition probabilities, conditional probabilities, and confidence layers at each time step using user-defined parameters such as dampening factors and divergence settings. Outputs include full time-series probability layers, BULC classification layers, confidence maps, and comparison layers, which are optionally exported to Google Drive or Earth Engine assets. The analysis supports both supervised and unsupervised modes, with detailed logging of pixel counts, proportions, and internal states for validation.

task:
Task: Compute cross-ratio over cultivated barley plots
Compute the mean VH/VV cross-ratio (CR) index in decibel (dB) units over cultivated agricultural plots (barley) for each Sentinel-1 image acquired during defined crop seasons (e.g., Oct–Jul). It first converts VH and VV backscatter from dB to sigma-naught, computes the CR ratio (VH_sigma / VV_sigma), then converts the result back to dB. For each season (e.g., 2014–2015, ..., 2019–2020), it filters Sentinel-1 descending-orbit GRD images, identifies cultivated plots by selecting only those with non-zero production values in the column matching the *season’s ending year* (e.g., '2016' column for season ending in 2016-07-31), masks and reduces CR over those plots using mean reduction, and outputs a time-series FeatureCollection of date-tagged CR mean values — exported as CSV and visualized in a chart.

Task: Calculate temperature-based mortality risk
Calculate a temperature-derived mortality risk (MR) index using maximum daily surface air temperature (tasmax) from climate model simulations under the RCP85 scenario. The final output is a global ToE raster map exported annually from 2016 to 2089, indicating when climate-driven mortality risk significantly emerges from baseline variability.

Task: Resample and convert GLDAS rainfall to daily mm
Process GLDAS v2.1 surface rainfall data over a user-defined polygon from January 1, 2010, to January 3, 2010, clipping it to the region, adding daily date metadata, and resampling it to match CHIRPS spatial resolution (0.05°) using bilinear interpolation and reprojection. It converts rainfall units from kg/m²/s (equivalent to mm/s) to mm/day by multiplying by 86400, then computes temporal fractions of daily rainfall within each day. The output is an ImageCollection where each image has the original rainfall, converted mm/day band, and a normalized 'Temporalfraction' band representing intra-day distribution. The final output includes layered maps of original and resampled rainfall and a combined ImageCollection sorted by date for downstream use.

task:
Task: Identify climate change emergence
Analyze the emergence of significant climate change signals in precipitation data from the NASA NEX-GDDP dataset under the RCP85 scenario using the CSIRO-Mk3-6-0 model. It calculates standardized anomalies by comparing decadal mean precipitation (2006–2089) against a baseline (inicial) and threshold (dis_max), then identifies years when anomalies exceed ±50% thresholds. These binary conditions are remapped to year labels (e.g., 16 for 2016), combined into an image collection, and reduced using min() to determine the earliest year of emergence. The output is a raster map indicating the first year when significant climate departure occurs, exported at 30 km resolution.

Analyze temporal changes in surface backscatter from Sentinel-1 VV-polarized SAR imagery over South Dakota, USA, to detect surface moisture variations between wet and dry periods. It computes the mean VV backscatter for two time intervals (wet: 2019-09-09 to 2019-09-15; dry: 2019-09-16 to 2019-09-26), calculates the difference (T2-T1) to highlight areas of increased or decreased moisture, and visualizes the change using a red-white-grey palette and a false-color RGB composite (Blue=T1, Red=T2). A refined Lee filter is defined but not applied in the final outputs. The primary outputs are three map layers: dry condition (T1), wet condition (T2), and their difference (Changes8bit and ChangesRGB), enabling qualitative assessment of surface moisture dynamics.

Task: Analyze NDVI trend rate
Analyze the temporal trend of EVI2 (a vegetation index similar to NDVI) from 2002 to 2016 using a Mann-Kendall non-parametric test for monotonic trends. It computes the Z-statistic to identify significantly increasing or decreasing trends, masks non-significant pixels, performs linear regression on the significant time series to estimate slope (k), and calculates relative change as (slope × number of years) / mean EVI2. The output is a raster map of relative change in vegetation condition over time, scaled and exported to Drive and Earth Engine Asset.

Task: Calculate dry days from precipitation data

Outputs are visualized using a color palette indicating increasing dryness and added to the map as layers labeled 'gddp' and 'persiann'.

task:
Task: Classify global thermal zones
Classify Earth's surface into combined thermal bioclimatic zones by integrating two distinct temperature-derived indices: (1) a 'warm zone' classification based on the hottest monthly mean air temperature (from WORLDCLIM BIO05 and ERA5), binned into 12 ordinal categories (1–12) representing summer heat intensity; and (2) a 'cold zone' classification based on the coldest monthly mean air temperature (from WORLDCLIM BIO06 and ERA5), binned into 9 ordinal categories (2–10) representing winter cold severity. Antarctica is treated separately using higher-resolution ERA5 monthly data, while the rest of the globe uses coarser WORLDCLIM V1 bioclimatic variables. The final output is a single integer 'combinedZone' raster layer where each pixel value = warmZone × 10 + coldZone (e.g., warm=7, cold=4 → code=74), visualized with a custom cyclic rainbow palette and interactive legend/tooltip displaying both component codes and their alphanumeric equivalents (e.g., 'B2', 'C').

task:
Task: Count annual frost days
Compute the number of frost days (days when minimum 2m air temperature falls below 0°C) for Finland (implied by ROI filtering with GAUL level0 and point location near 25.17°E, 63.79°N — consistent with Finnish territory) using ERA5 daily reanalysis data. It first calculates frost occurrence per day (binary mask), sums across days to get total frost days for 2018–2019 (single-year composite), then extends the workflow to generate an annual time series (1980–2020) of frost-day counts per year. Outputs include: (1) a clipped raster layer 'frost_2018' showing frost-day count for 2018–2019 (note: despite variable name '2018', time filter is 2018–2019, but ERA5 DAILY has calendar-year-aligned files; actual interpretation is 2018 only — see time range analysis); (2) a Chart.image.series plot of mean frost days over Finland per year (1980–2020); (3) a multi-band image 'finland_frost_years' where each band is named 'frost_days_YYYY' representing the annual frost-day count raster for that year; and (4) corresponding Drive exports for both single-year and multi-year composites.

Task: Compute NDVI-based composite
Compute a time-series composite image representing the mean reflectance values (and NDVI) from the top 20% of Landsat 8 surface reflectance observations ranked by descending NDVI at a single point location. It first preprocesses Landsat 8 Level 2 surface reflectance images (applying QA masking, radiometric scaling, and NDVI calculation), filters to a six-month period (Jan–Jun 2021) over a point in the San Francisco Bay Area, converts the collection to an array, sorts pixel-wise observations by NDVI, selects the highest 20% NDVI instances per pixel, and reduces them to a single multi-band image (with SR_B4, SR_B5, SR_B6, and NDVI) representing the mean of those high-vegetation-condition observations — intended for visualization and analysis of peak vegetation spectral response.

task:
Task: Map severe vegetation loss
the workflow quantifies and maps areas of severe vegetation loss in Majuli Island, Assam, India, for the year 2022 by computing NDVI change between pre-monsoon (Mar–May) and post-monsoon (Aug–Nov) periods using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data. It computes short-term NDVI (using median composites from two narrow seasonal windows), falls back to long-term seasonal medians (Jan–Jun and Jul–Dec) where short-term data is masked, calculates NDVI difference (ΔNDVI), applies a strict threshold (ΔNDVI < −0.25) to isolate severe loss, and visualizes the resulting binary mask overlaid on true-color and NDVI-change layers. Output is a spatially explicit, masked raster layer highlighting locations of major vegetation collapse.

task:
Task: Estimate soil moisture from SAR data
Estimate surface soil moisture (SM) over agricultural fields in Machakos using C-band Sentinel-1 GRD imagery. It processes VV and VH polarized backscatter, applies speckle filtering with a boxcar kernel, computes polarization ratios and angular transformations, and integrates empirical models (e.g., Srivastava et al., 2008) to derive a Soil Roughness (SR) proxy. A multi-step physical-empirical model is then applied involving radar scattering components, incidence angle corrections, and wavelength-based constants to compute a final Soil Moisture Index (SM). The output is a continuous raster map of estimated soil moisture values within the region of interest, visualized with a color palette and centered on the study area in the map viewer.

task:
Task: Filter RVI time series
Compute the Radar Vegetation Index (RVI) from Sentinel-1 GRD backscatter imagery (VV and VH polarizations) over a defined polygon in Iran (inferred from coordinates ~48.6°E, 31.0°N), then applies a temporal speckle filter using a 15-day sliding window mean via an image collection join. It outputs two layers: (1) the raw RVI time series (unfiltered), and (2) the temporally smoothed 'corrected' RVI layer where each image is replaced by the mean RVI of all images within ±7.5 days — effectively reducing speckle noise while preserving temporal structure. The workflow includes radiometric calibration (converting dB to linear sigma0), RVI expression ((4 × VH) / (VH + VV)), property preservation across mapping operations, and visualization-ready clipped band stacks.

task:
Task: Model urban land change over time
the workflow models land use and land cover (LULC) change over time using a Bayesian Updating of Land Cover (BULC) framework. It starts with a base land cover image from 2000 and sequentially integrates 20 years of classified event images (e.g., k-means clustered time series) to update per-pixel class probabilities. The workflow uses transition probability matrices, prior distributions from initial conditions, and conditional likelihoods derived from event inputs to compute daily posterior probabilities. Key outputs include time-series BULC classifications, confidence layers, conditional probabilities, and event-based change layers. Final outputs are exported as multi-band probability rasters for analysis, supporting long-term urban or built-up land dynamics assessment in Zambia.

task:
Task: Estimate daily runoff using SCS-CN method
Estimate daily surface runoff in the Klip River Catchment (South Africa) using the Soil Conservation Service Curve Number (SCS-CN) method. It derives land use/land cover from MODIS MCD12Q1 and soil texture from OpenLandMap to compute curve numbers (CN1, CN2, CN3) and potential retention (S). Daily rainfall data from CHIRPS is used to calculate antecedent moisture conditions (AMC) over a 5-day moving window. Runoff is computed using a conditional expression based on precipitation and variable S values adjusted by AMC class, with outputs including time-series runoff images, cumulative rainfall and runoff maps, and interactive charts for the catchment. The final output is an ImageCollection of daily runoff rasters and a combined Rainfall-Runoff time series chart.

task:
Task: Estimate land surface temperature
Estimate land surface temperature (LST) for the Xiamen region using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data from May to September 2020. It applies cloud masking to the imagery, computes NDVI to derive fractional vegetation cover (FVC), calculates surface emissivity, and finally retrieves LST using a radiative transfer-based algorithm involving Band 10 brightness temperature and emissivity correction. Outputs include min, max, mean, and standard deviation of LST over the region, a false-color LST map visualized with a temperature-appropriate palette, and export of the LST raster to Google Drive.

task:
Task: Compare depth estimates from multiple sensors
Compare bathymetric depth estimates derived from three different sources—Sentinel-2 imagery processed by Dimos, EOMAP's SDB product, and Planet Dove high-tide imagery—over the Cairns-Cooktown area in the Great Barrier Reef. It loads and preprocesses depth rasters by standardizing band names and applying sign inversion where necessary. The core workflow stacks these depth layers into a multi-band image and enables interactive transect-based spatial profiling using a custom drawing tool. When a user draws a transect on the map, the workflow extracts mean depth values along the line at 10-meter sampling intervals using ee.Reducer.mean(), then generates a comparative depth profile chart with distance on the x-axis and depth on the y-axis, color-coded by source. The output includes an interactive visualization panel with layered maps and a dynamic chart display embedded in a split UI layout for real-time analysis.

Task: Compute GRACE-informed groundwater anomaly
Compute annual soil moisture (or snow water equivalent) anomalies relative to the 2003–2016 mean for three HUC-04 basins in California's Central Valley (HUC codes 1802, 1803, 1804), using GLDAS Noah model output. It selects a specified variable band (default 'SWE_inst', but annotated for adjustment to 'SM_inst'), filters the NASA/GLDAS/V021/NOAH/G025/T3H hourly 0.25° dataset to the time range and basin geometry, computes the long-term mean image, then calculates the deviation of a single-year (2003) mean image from that climatology — resulting in an anomaly image labeled with year and system:time_start, which is exported to Google Earth Engine Assets as 'swe2003' (though intended for SM). The workflow is explicitly designed for groundwater storage change inference via terrestrial water storage components, per the GRACE monitoring context.

task:
Task: Extract Sentinel-2 texture features
Process Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from August 2020 over a user-defined region (ROI2), applying cloud masking using the QA60 band to remove pixels affected by clouds and cirrus. It selects specific 20m-resolution bands (B5, B6, B7, B8A, B11, B12), resamples them to 10m resolution via bilinear interpolation, and reprojects them to EPSG:32648. These are then combined with native 10m bands (B2, B3, B4, B8) to create a multispectral image stack at uniform 10m resolution. Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture features are computed from this composite using Earth Engine's glcmTexture() function, resulting in multiple textural layers (e.g., contrast, entropy, homogeneity). The output includes the original RGB visualization, the full GLCM texture layer set clipped to ROI2, and an export task to save the processed S2_08 image (including spectral and texture bands) as a GeoTIFF asset. This workflow supports detailed land cover analysis based on both spectral and spatial texture information.

Task: Extract daily hydroclimate variables for streamflow modeling
Extract daily time-series hydroclimatic variables over the Yampa River Basin at Deerlodge Park for use as inputs to a streamflow model. It computes basin-wide and elevation-band-specific (three equal-area bands derived from SRTM DEM percentiles) statistics from NASA/ORNL DAYMET_V4 data, including mean temperature (°C), precipitation (mm/day), shortwave radiation (W/m²), and snow water equivalent (mm). Task: Extract vegetation and water indices
Compute multiple spectral indices related to vegetation, water, built-up areas, and soil from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data over a user-defined region of interest (roi). It processes the imagery by applying cloud masking and scaling factors, filters for specific months, and calculates median composites. The key outputs include NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, NDMI, SAVI, EVI, MNDWI, LSWI, AWEI, WRI, CMRI, MAWEI, MVI, RVI, and NDSSI, which are added as bands to a multi-layered image. Additionally, elevation, slope, seafloor topography (ETOPO1), and sea surface salinity (SSS) are integrated. These layers are visualized on the map and printed as a combined Earth Engine image for potential use in land cover or environmental monitoring analysis.

task:
Task: Compute TVMDI index
Compute the Temperature-Vegetation Moisture Dryness Index (TVMDI) by combining normalized time-series MODIS-derived land surface temperature (LST), vegetation condition (PVI), and moisture condition (SM) over a specified geometry. Each variable is scaled using min-max normalization and transformed into a common index space. The final TVMDI is derived through a composite formula involving squared terms of SM and LST and subtracted PVI contribution, followed by clamping values between 0 and 1. Outputs include a time-composited TVMDI raster map, exported to Google Drive, and associated charts for temporal trends of the input variables.

Task: Classify land cover in Hwange
Classify land cover in the Hwange district of Zimbabwe using Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 satellite imagery combined with SRTM elevation and slope data from 2020. It computes median spectral bands from Sentinel-2 (B8, B5, B4), generates radar percentile and interquartile range features from Sentinel-1 (VV and VH polarizations), and incorporates terrain variables (elevation and slope). These features form an input stack for a pre-existing classification image ('HWANGE_Edit'), which is then refined through a series of manual corrections using vector-based rules to reassign misclassified pixels (e.g., changing class 2 to 4, 5 to 1, etc.). The final output is a corrected land cover map with 8 distinct classes, visualized with a custom color palette, intended for spatial analysis of land cover patterns in the region.

Task: Classify land cover using SNIC segments
Classify land cover in the Nipigon region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from June to September 2018. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band, computes median composites, and segments the image using SNIC (Superpixel Neighbors for Image Clustering) with a 9-meter seed grid. Per-segment statistics (mean, standard deviation, area) are calculated, and a Random Forest classifier is trained on seeded regions using reference data (SOLRIS) within geometry2. The final classification is applied to SNIC objects, clipped to geometry3, and exported as a raster. Outputs include a classified land cover map of segmented objects and derived property layers (means, std dev, area) for analysis.

Task: Map surface water frequency
Map the frequency of surface water occurrence (as percent of cloud-free observations) over a Landsat WRS path/row tile intersecting a user-defined point geometry in Louisiana (approx. -93.65°, 31.32°). It processes Landsat 5 TM, 7 ETM+, and 8 OLI Surface Reflectance (SR) collections (1980–2017), applies cloud masking using cfmask, classifies water using a fixed threshold (B5 < 500) on the SWIR band, computes per-pixel count and mean of classified water pixels across all valid scenes, normalizes counts to percentage, filters out low-frequency events (<20%), and exports a masked mean reflectance raster (B1) where only pixels with ≥20% water occurrence are retained — effectively producing a persistent surface water frequency map. Outputs include a classified raster for visualization/export and a CSV metadata table listing scene names, cloud cover, and summed pixel values over a user-defined polygon.

Task: Calculate plant productivity index
Calculate a daily Enhanced Productivity Index (EPI) for the year 2001, combining temperature, precipitation, photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), and soil water availability. It uses GLDAS temperature data, PERSIANN precipitation, BESS PAR, and USDA soil texture to derive intermediate indices (It, Ip, Iw) based on empirical equations, then multiplies them and scales by a constant (Pm=40) to estimate potential plant productivity in mg/ha/y. The final output is a mean annual productivity image exported to Google Drive.

Task: Detect landslide-prone areas using SAR amplitude change

It computes the difference in median VH backscatter between pre-event (2021-01-01 to 2021-06-29) and post-event (2021-07-09 to 2021-12-29) periods for both ascending and descending orbits, averages the amplitude ratios, and applies slope and curvature masks derived from SRTM to focus on steep, convex terrain. Outputs include layered visualizations of pre/post-event amplitude stacks, amplitude ratio maps (masked and unmasked), and exports the final amplitude change raster as a GeoTIFF for further analysis.

task:
Task: Classify future aridity and climate regimes
Classify global terrestrial climate regimes for the year 2100 under RCP8.5 emissions scenario using NASA/NEX-GDDP downscaled GCM data. It computes monthly climatologies of precipitation (PR), maximum/minimum temperature (TASMAX/TASMIN), derives mean temperature in °C, calculates potential evapotranspiration (PET) via a simplified Penman–Monteith–derived expression using saturation vapor pressure and extraterrestrial radiation, computes annual precipitation (P_ann) and PET (PET_ann), calculates Aridity Index (AI = P/PET), applies validity constraints (coldest month ≥ –20 °C and hottest month ≥ 15 °C), assigns base aridity classes (0–3), then distinguishes monsoon (W) vs. Mediterranean (M) regimes based on high-sun season (Apr–Sep) precipitation fraction (HS_ratio), and flips the monsoon/Mediterranean labels in the Southern Hemisphere to account for reversed seasonal insolation. The final output is a global raster map of six climate classes (D, S, G, H, W, M) visualized with a custom palette and interactive point query.

task:
Task: Pansharpen Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery
the workflow performs pansharpening on both a median-composite Landsat 8 TOA reflectance image (from 2016) and a specific Sentinel-2 image (from 2020) over the same region. For Landsat, it implements a custom neighborhood-based mean-preserving fusion method using a square kernel (90m radius), then reprojects and exports the sharpened result at 15m resolution in UTM Zone 23S (EPSG:31983). For Sentinel-2, it applies a high-pass filter-based sharpening algorithm that fuses 20m multispectral bands with 10m panchromatic information using statistical matching, producing a fused image where all bands are effectively enhanced to 10m resolution. The outputs include visualizations of original and sharpened composites for both sensors and an export task for the pansharpened Landsat composite.

Task: Classify land cover change
Analyze land surface changes between January 2021 and January 2022 using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery over a defined geometry. It applies cloud masking via QA60 band filtering and computes spectral indices (NDVI, NDSI, BI) to support change detection. A Sobel edge detector (Hv, Hh kernels) and SAM (Spectral Angle Mapper) are used for difference analysis. Shadow masks are generated using brightness and NDVI thresholds. Validation is performed using independent samples, generating error matrices and overall accuracy metrics. Outputs include classified rasters for both dates, change layers (difference, SAM), shadow masks, and accuracy assessments for land cover change modeling.

Task: Analyze land surface temperature anomaly
Analyze land surface temperature (LST) changes in the Krasnoyarskiy Kray region of Russia using MODIS MOD11A2 data. It computes the median daytime LST over two periods: a baseline period from 2010 to 2019 and a target year in 2011, both restricted to day-of-year 90–151 (April to early July). The baseline is averaged across years, while the 2011 image is a single-year mean. Both are masked to the Krasnoyarsk region, converted from digital numbers to Celsius, and used to compute a temperature anomaly map (2011 minus baseline). The output includes three visual maps: baseline LST, 2011 LST, and LST anomaly, with interactive visualization and a custom legend for the anomaly layer.

Task: Identify surface water extent
Identify surface water extent in a region using Landsat 7 and 8 surface reflectance imagery from 2019. It applies cloud masking using pixel quality bands (pixel_qa) for both sensors, merges the collections, and computes a median composite. A threshold-based transformation ('trend') is applied to derive a binary mask (mememe) where negative values indicate potential water bodies. The Joint Research Centre's Global Surface Water (JRC GSW) dataset for 2019 is then clipped and compared, with water class 3 (permanent water) extracted as reference. The output includes a classified water map (JRC), a derived water mask (mememe), and a multi-band feature image (images) combining optical, thermal, terrain, and texture layers for potential use in water classification modeling.

Task: Identify burned forest areas
Identify burned forest areas using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from May 2019. It applies cloud masking via QA60 band, computes multiple spectral indices (NDVI, NBR, NBR2, MIRBI, TBR, BAI, BAI2, TGR, TWT), masks water and non-forest areas using ALOS PALSAR forest/non-forest map, and applies a two-stage thresholding approach: first using BAI and TBR, then refining with NDVI and NBR. The output includes burned area mosaics for four weekly periods, final burned area maps, and quantitative estimates of burned area in square meters derived from pixel counts. Validation is performed by comparing with FireCCI51 and MCD64A1 burned area products.

Task: Detect vegetation loss using SAR

task:
Task: Estimate NPP from FAPAR and solar radiation
Estimate Net Primary Productivity (NPP) by combining Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR), derived from Landsat 8 NDVI and SR (Surface Reflectance ratio), with surface solar radiation from ERA5-Land reanalysis data. FAPAR is computed using a linear transformation of NDVI and a derived SR band, then combined monthly with downscaled solar radiation. APAR (Absorbed PAR) is calculated as half the product of solar radiation and FAPAR, and NPP is modeled as the product of APAR and an assumed light use efficiency (E, not defined in script). Outputs include a time-series ImageCollection of NPP, which is printed, visualized, and intended for export, though the export fails due to未defined variables (ndvimin, ndvimax, SRmin, SRmax, E, Topt).

The Bmax method computes optimal thresholds per image tile with an initial threshold of -17 dB, while the Edge method enhances edge-based segmentation with 300m smoothing. task:
Task: Compute TVMDI index
Compute the Temperature-Vegetation Moisture Dryness Index (TVMDI) by combining normalized time-series of land surface temperature (LST), vegetation condition (PVI), and moisture condition (SM) derived from MODIS imagery over a specified geometry. It first processes MOD11A2 LST data for daytime values, scales them, and filters valid observations. Then, it calculates PVI and SM indices from MYD09A1 surface reflectance bands, normalizes each index using min-max scaling multiplied by a factor of 0.57735, converts them into band-stacked images, and finally computes TVMDI as the square root of the sum of squared SM and LST components minus the square of PVI plus a constant (0.33), clamped between 0 and 1. Outputs include a time series chart of normalized LST, PVI, and SM, the final TVMDI raster, and exports it to Google Drive.

Compute the percentage change (as standardized anomalies: (projection − baseline_mean) / baseline_stdDev) in climate indicator (pr, tasmax, or tasmin) between a historical baseline period and a future projection period, aggregated over a user-specified season (month range). It processes CMIP6 model ensemble data from NASA/GDDP-CMIP6, computes per-model annual sums for both periods, derives baseline mean and standard deviation per model, then calculates standardized anomalies for the projection period. Finally, it aggregates across all 22 GCMs to produce ensemble median, 25th, and 75th percentile statistics — resulting in a single ee.Image with bands: 'indicator_median', 'indicator_p25', 'indicator_p75'.

task:
Task: Detect vegetation loss using SAR backscatter change
Detect vegetation loss over a user-defined region (roi/stats_area/newroi) by analyzing temporal changes in Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter intensity (VV and VH polarizations) for three years: 2016, 2018, and 2019. It loads, filters, and mosaics GRD imagery; applies focal mean filtering (50 m radius) to suppress speckle; computes difference (not ratio — despite misleading variable names like 'ratio1618VH') images between years (2016–2018 and 2018–2019) for VH and VV; calculates statistics (mean, std dev) over newroi; applies fixed empirical thresholds (2.35 and 2.95) to the VH difference images to generate binary vegetation loss masks; computes and prints pixel-count-based area estimates of loss within stats_area; and visualizes all intermediate and final products (filtered images, difference layers, thresholded masks) on the map. Critically, the analysis relies on the principle that vegetation loss (e.g., deforestation, agricultural conversion) increases surface roughness and decreases volume scattering, leading to increased VH backscatter — hence positive differences (2016 VH − 2018 VH > threshold) indicate loss between those years.

Task: Map seasonal water extent using MNDWI

It computes the MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index) from atmospherically corrected surface reflectance data, applies cloud masking specific to Landsat 4/5/7 and Landsat 8, and generates composite images for wet (June–October) and dry (November–May) seasons. A time series of annual water area (in km²) is computed using the 98th percentile MNDWI threshold for 2021, producing a bar chart showing total water surface area per year.

Task: Identify urban expansion and renewal
Analyze land development intensity (LDI) using Landsat 5 TOA imagery from 1996 and 1997 over a specific fishnet grid (Id10 = 168). It computes the ratio of near-infrared (B3) to blue (B1) bands as a spectral index (CLI) for both years, calculates LDI as the ratio of post-to-pre development CLI, and identifies land development with a threshold (>1.1). Water and vegetation masks derived from NDWI and NDVI are used to exclude non-urban land covers. Morphological filtering (focal_mode) refines the binary outputs. task:
Task: Track urban land change over time
the workflow performs a Bayesian Updating of Land Cover (BULC) analysis to model land cover change over time using a sequence of event images derived from satellite data. It starts with a base land cover image from 2000 and processes biannual event layers (e.g., 1999–2003) to iteratively update probabilities of land cover class transitions. The workflow includes handling conditional probabilities, tracking maximum likelihood classes (BULC classification), and recording confidence (maximum probability) at each time step. Key outputs include time-series BULC classifications, probability layers, confidence maps, conditional probabilities, and comparison layers, all exported based on user-defined settings. The analysis supports both supervised and unsupervised modes, with options to export multi-band rasters for visualization and further analysis.

task:
Task: Calculate vegetation productivity index
Calculate a modified EPI (Ecological Productivity Index) using daily meteorological and soil data from GLDAS, PERSIANN-CDR, and BESS datasets over a specified time period. It first aggregates hourly temperature (Tmax and Tmin), surface radiation (Swnet_tavg), precipitation, and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) to daily values, then combines them with USDA soil texture data to compute intermediate indices (It, Ip, Iw) based on empirical equations. The final EPI is derived as the product of these indices normalized by days in month and scaled by a constant (Pm=46), resulting in an estimated productivity in Mg/ha. The output is a mean annual productivity map at 0.25° resolution, reduced from the daily ImageCollection, which is visualized and added to the map.
